title: Compose the ordered setup command over the existing primitives
statement: Implement `bin/setup.mjs` running the ordered phases: path resolution, Node validation, the setup lock, the locked dependency install, the dynamic imports, the transaction plan, initialization, the project ID and state protection, the journal, trust, package registration, consent, model binding, credential contract, research choice, preflight, canary and read-back — with every installed dependency imported dynamically after the install step, and no second initializer.
notes:
⚠️ R9 IS SETUP'S (recorded 2026-09-13). The skill-override entry `../planning-content/skills-overrides` is fixed relative to `.pi`, while the content root can be selected elsewhere, for example through `PLANNING_CONTENT_DIR`. Setup owns making the entry it writes agree with the selected content root's `skills-overrides/`. TSK-0047 proves the entry only in the default layout, where the content root is `<project>/planning-content`.

⚠️ STAGE-DOCUMENT MIGRATION IS SETUP'S (recorded 2026-09-18, TSK-0049). `kiln_write_stage_document` writes into a `## Intake` section with two anchored regions, and refuses a document that does not have them rather than upgrading one during a write: a write is not the moment to restructure a document somebody may have edited. Projects initialized before that section existed therefore cannot record an answer until their stage documents carry it. Setup owns adding it, the same way it owns making the skill-override entry agree with the selected content root. Kiln's own Stage 1 document was migrated by hand as a one-off and is not the general answer.

⚠️ THE ORDER IS D26 (2026-09-22): paths, Node, lock, install, dynamic imports, plan, initializer, project ID and state protection, journal, then the remaining phases. The dependency install comes before the transaction plan because the plan validates existing Kiln records, and that validation needs Ajv, which the install is what provides. Everything up to and including the install is therefore built-ins only (ACC-0083), and the install is a bootstrap mutation confined to the .planning checkout: it changes no consumer project state and does not rewrite the lockfile. ⚠️ SLICE 1 LANDED 2026-09-22 (EVD-0133, commits e808b96 and 7ef9d4d). bin/setup.mjs runs D26's order as far as the journal: the five paths printed before any mutation, the engines check, the single lock held for the whole run, `npm ci --ignore-scripts` confined to this checkout, the dynamic imports, the transaction plan, and the phases state-coverage, initialize, state-protection and project-identity before the journal opens. Two review findings were closed in 7ef9d4d: the .gitignore fix now runs inside the planned transaction as a declared phase rather than before it, and the bootstrap install is locked and runs no dependency lifecycle script. ACC-0083 passes from that evidence. STILL OWED HERE: slice 2 (Pi import and version verification, trust, package registration, the skill-override entry agreeing with the selected content root — R9 above), slice 3 (consent, discovery, selection, the credential contract, research) and slice 4 (preflight, the live model check, read-back, the full exit-code mapping and resume), plus `--local-state user`, which refuses by name in slice 1. ACC-0085 waits until every supported state path is implemented; ACC-0043, ACC-0045, ACC-0106, ACC-0107 and ACC-0108 wait for the integration record after all slices land. ⚠️ REGISTRATION IS A PLANNED MERGE, NOT `pi install -l` (D27, 2026-09-22). Setup writes the package entry itself, through the transaction's own settings merge, and does not run `pi install -l` against the consumer project. `.pi/settings.json` is a planned target whose recorded identity is what makes the merge refuse a file that moved; `pi install -l` writes that file itself, so inside the plan it would have to be adopted — widening the rule that stops a concurrent edit being laundered into the plan — and outside the plan it would write a project file the transaction has not contained or probed. The portable entry `../.planning/pi-package` is written only after it is proved to resolve to this checkout's canonical package directory, and that the registered entry loads is proved by running pinned Pi against it. EVD-0079 and ACC-0105 remain the component proof of Pi's literal entry and its portable equivalent. Because the settings writer requires a provider, a model and a thinking level that are not chosen until slice 3, slice 2 writes through a package-and-skill-only merge that preserves existing defaults and every unrelated setting. ⚠️ SLICE 2 LANDED 2026-09-22 (commits 309e26c and b1d455e). The pinned Pi version is verified immediately after the dynamic imports and before the transaction plan; the trust decision is obtained and never assumed, with `--trust approve|deny` answering over a recorded decision and only an explicit no recording a denial; and Kiln's package and the content root's skill overrides are registered through a package-and-skill-only merge that leaves every other setting alone. ⚠️ **R9 IS STILL OPEN.** The skill-override entry is now derived from the resolved content root and proved to resolve back to it, instead of being a fixed spelling — but the command refuses every content root other than `<project>/planning-content`, because `initializeProject` creates that one by its own single rule and a run that accepted another selection would print one content root and create a second. R9 is closed only when setup can own a content root the initializer does not create; until then the derivation is proved at the unit level and the command's behaviour is the refusal. ⚠️ OWED BY THE EXIT-CODE MAPPING (2026-09-22, narrowed after slice 3): every Kiln refusal class now prints as the written refusal it carries — slice 3 gave `reportFailure` a branch for them — so a registration refusal no longer reaches the operator as a stack trace. What remains is the classification: `PackageEntryRefusal`, `SettingsRefusal`, `ModelSelectionRefusal` and the rest all exit with the generic setup code. Which code each deserves is the mapping this task publishes. ⚠️ SLICE 3 LANDED 2026-09-22 (EVD-0135, commits 4313e6e and 5aaa2da). Inspection consent precedes every read of this host — and, since 3317fff, every touch of the environment: loading Pi's SDK enumerates it, so the trust decision, which the proposal orders first, is taken in a child whose environment is built by naming variables, and this process loads no Pi until the operator has allowed it — model discovery and selection run through the existing writers so a changed choice clears the previous grant before the new selection is written, the selected provider's credential contract is resolved from Kiln's table, and the research decision is settled separately. An answer the command cannot read is never recorded as a decision, a run with nobody to ask does not ask, and a partial setup exits 9 with a valid project. STILL OWED: slice 4 (the preflight canary, the live model check, read-back, resume and the full exit-code mapping), R9's content root, custom-provider credential inputs (D25, D13) and `--local-state user`. ⚠️ SLICE 4 LANDED 2026-09-23 (EVD-0136, commit 7d0d48a). The zero-cost preflight runs before anything billable is offered, the live model check has its own approval (`--live-model-check approve|deny`, a prompt, or a refusal when there is nobody to ask), the compatibility record is read back and compared against the key recomputed from what Pi resolved before any readiness is reported, an interrupted run is continued only with `--resume`, and `--help` publishes every exit code. STILL OWED BY THIS TASK: R9's alternate content root, custom-provider credential inputs (D25, D13), `--local-state user`, and narrowing the refusal classes that still share the generic setup exit code. The spanning criteria stay not-evaluated until those land and the integration record is written. ⚠️ SLICE 5 LANDED 2026-09-23 (EVD-0137, commits 0a325c7, 2c61a1b and 804dd43), closing what the earlier slices owed: R9's alternate content root (the initializer takes an explicit root contained in the project and stages beside it; setup initializes there and says later runs need the same selection), `--local-state user` (the external root is keyed by the committed id, which is committed first in a transaction planning that record alone), the custom-provider credential inputs (`--credential-var NAME`, a name and never a value, with the canary given the provider's non-credential configuration and exercised for real against a loopback endpoint), and one published exit code per refusal class. WHAT REMAINS FOR THIS TASK: the integrated acceptance evidence, from which ACC-0043, ACC-0045, ACC-0085, ACC-0106, ACC-0107 and ACC-0108 can be evaluated. ⚠️ INTEGRATED 2026-09-23 (EVD-0138, at 9510d6e). All six spanning criteria are evaluated and pass: ACC-0043, ACC-0045, ACC-0085, ACC-0106, ACC-0107 and ACC-0108. The integrated measurement found and fixed a defect of its own: a killed run's lockfile made every rerun wait out the two-minute stale window. REVIEW FOUND A SECOND DEFECT IN THE FIX, THE CONTROL FOR IT FOUND A THIRD IN CI, AND REVIEW OF THAT FIX FOUND A FOURTH; three criteria were also withdrawn while their controls were repaired and restored only after. All four lock defects are one mistake at four depths — judging a file and then removing it. Breaking a lock is now serialised behind a gate beside it, taken by the recovery path and the waiter's stale break alike; reclaiming an abandoned gate is serialised by a token; and the token is never reclaimed, so a run killed inside that window fails closed: exit 17, with both files named. The repairs: ACC-0045 parses the resume arguments out of the recorded command rather than typing them beside it; ACC-0106 takes its file set from a NUL-delimited before/after boundary with no exemption list and checks absolute paths by shape as well as by value; ACC-0108 serves the browser-only route against the denied project and asserts a rendered page. ONE LIMIT REMAINS: `npm start`'s production path, which installs and builds before serving, is not exercised, because no billable request or registry install happens anywhere in the suite.
